svg.title: Multi-tenant isolation — additive migration and deny-all row-level security
svg.desc: An additive schema migration introduces a tenant table and a membership table, adds a tenant foreign key to each operational table, backfills the existing client as tenant one, and scopes uniqueness per tenant instead of globally. Deny-all row-level security is enabled on the new tables with service-role-only access, and console auth is fail-closed asymmetric-key validation with an administrator allow-list. Two operational rules are called out: swapping a uniqueness constraint silently breaks the write path because the upsert helper still names the old conflict target, so schema and code ship as one atomic deploy with a rollback script written before the migration runs; and read-path scoping is deliberately deferred while there is a single tenant, but recorded as a hard prerequisite before a second tenant is onboarded, not as a nice-to-have.
svg.text: Additive migration — nothing dropped, nothing renamed
tenant
new — existing client backfilled as #1
membership
user ↔ tenant, with role
operational tables
each gains a tenant foreign key; uniqueness re-scoped per tenant
conversations
cases
review queue
documents
events
delivery meter
delivery metering is idempotent by a uniqueness constraint, and wrapped so that
a metering failure can never block a delivery
Access control
deny-all row-level security on every new table
no policy grants the anonymous or authenticated role
any access at all; the service role bypasses RLS and is
the only path in. Anonymous access verified denied.
console auth: fail-closed asymmetric-key validation
with an administrator allow-list
The constraint swap that breaks the write path
Changing a uniqueness constraint silently breaks every
write whose upsert helper still names the old conflict
target. Schema change and code change therefore ship as
ONE atomic deploy — rollback script written first.
The deliberately deferred part
Read-path scoping is a no-op with a single tenant, so it
was not done in this change. It is written down as a HARD
PREREQUISITE before a second tenant is onboarded.
A deferred correctness property that is not written down
as a blocker is a bug with a delay fuse.
